Tidy and plot a TVP-VAR

Source: R/tvp-plot.R
tidy.tvpvar.Rd

tidy() summarises the posterior paths through time as a tibble: type = "coef" gives date, response (equation), term, estimate (posterior median), conf.low, conf.high; "vol" and "shock_vol" give date, variable, estimate, conf.low, conf.high for the reduced-form residual and the orthogonalised shock standard deviations (tvp_volatility()). glance() is a one-row summary.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
tidy(
  x,
  type = c("coef", "vol", "shock_vol"),
  equation = NULL,
  level = 0.68,
  const = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
as_tibble(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
autoplot(
  object,
  type = c("coef", "vol", "shock_vol", "irf"),
  equation = NULL,
  level = 0.68,
  const = FALSE,
  shock = NULL,
  response = NULL,
  horizon = c(0L, 4L, 8L),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar_path'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar'
plot(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tvpvar_path'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x, object

a tvpvar() fit.

type

"coef", "vol", "shock_vol" (and "irf" for autoplot()).

equation

<tidy-select> equation(s) for type = "coef". tidy() defaults to all, autoplot() to the first.

level

credible level of the band.

const

include the intercept path (type = "coef").

...

unused (plot() passes them to autoplot()).

shock, response

<tidy-select> variables of the response shown by type = "irf".

horizon

horizons of the response shown by type = "irf".

Value

tidy(), glance(): a tibble; autoplot(): a ggplot.

Details

autoplot() draws the paths with their credible band (type = "coef", "vol", "shock_vol") or the response of response to shock through time at the given horizons (type = "irf", via irf_path()).

See also

Other TVP-VAR: irf_path(), tvp_dynamics, tvp_prior(), tvp_volatility(), tvpvar()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- tvpvar(yraw, p = 2, ndraw = 200, nburn = 200)
tidy(fit, "vol")
#> # A tibble: 519 × 5
#>     date variable estimate conf.low conf.high
#>    <int> <fct>       <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1    43 infl        0.234    0.181     0.303
#>  2    44 infl        0.240    0.183     0.305
#>  3    45 infl        0.241    0.180     0.299
#>  4    46 infl        0.242    0.180     0.295
#>  5    47 infl        0.247    0.188     0.308
#>  6    48 infl        0.245    0.192     0.303
#>  7    49 infl        0.244    0.194     0.306
#>  8    50 infl        0.248    0.196     0.311
#>  9    51 infl        0.251    0.199     0.305
#> 10    52 infl        0.253    0.209     0.311

autoplot(fit, "coef", equation = infl)
